outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Tabular Learning and Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the fundamental concepts of tabular learning and explores the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance this field, particularly in scenarios with limited data.
subtopics: What is Tabular Learning?
The Challenge of Few-Shot Learning in Tabular Data
The Role of Prior Knowledge in Machine Learning
Overview of LLMs: From Text Generation to Reasoning
Comparing Traditional Tabular Models with LLM-based Approaches

outline.description: Before diving into the proposed solution, this chapter analyzes why using LLMs as direct predictors for every single data sample is impractical for real-world tabular tasks.
subtopics: The End-to-End Prediction Pipeline
Computational Cost and Inference Latency
The 'Lost in the Middle' Phenomenon: Prompt Size Limitations
Dependency on Fine-Tuning vs. API-level Access
The Need for a Shift from Predictor to Feature Engineer

outline.description: This chapter provides a high-level introduction to the FeatLLM framework, explaining the core philosophy of using LLMs to discover 'rules' rather than predict labels.
subtopics: The Core Idea: LLM as an Expert Feature Engineer
The FeatLLM Pipeline Architecture
Defining 'Rules' in the Context of Tabular Data
High-Level Workflow: Rule Extraction to Class Likelihood
Key Advantages: Inference Efficiency and Training-Free Feature Discovery

outline.description: A deep dive into the pedagogical approach used to guide the LLM toward generating high-quality, decisive rules for classification.
subtopics: Components of the Basic Information Description
The Power of Serialization: Converting Tables to Text
Structured Reasoning: The Two-Step Process
Step 1: Extracting Prior Knowledge and Causal Relationships
Step 2: Deriving Rules from Few-Shot Examples
Response Instructions and Formatting for Parsability

outline.chapter_title: Translating Natural Language Rules into Features
outline.description: This chapter explains the technical process of converting the LLM's textual rules into a binary feature matrix that a machine learning model can process.
subtopics: The Parsing Challenge: Dealing with Syntactic Noise
Leveraging LLMs for Code Generation
Implementing Rule Execution via Python's exec()
Creating Binary Feature Vectors (The Rule Matrix)
Mapping Natural Language Conditions to Logical Operators

outline.description: Once features are engineered, they must be used for prediction. This chapter explains the simple yet effective ML model used to estimate class likelihood.
subtopics: Linear Models for Binary Feature Sets
Learning Feature Importance via Trainable Weights
The Necessity of Non-Negative Weights
Computing Class Probabilities with the Softmax Function
Optimizing the Model using Cross-Entropy Loss in Few-Shot Regimes

outline.chapter_title: Scaling and Robustness: Bagging and Ensembling
outline.description: This chapter focuses on the strategies used to handle large feature sets and reduce the variance of the LLM's outputs.
subtopics: The Role of Randomness: Temperature and Demonstration Ordering
Feature Bagging: Overcoming Prompt Size Constraints
The Ensemble Process: Averaging Probabilities across Multiple Trials
Self-Consistency: Why Repeated Inferences Lead to Better Rules
Trade-offs Between the Number of Ensembles and Performance

outline.description: This chapter discusses the empirical evaluation of the framework, comparing it against a variety of traditional and modern baselines.
subtopics: Dataset Selection: From Real-World to Synthetic Data
Performance Metrics: Understanding AUC
Comparative Analysis: FeatLLM vs. TabLLM, TabPFN, and XGBoost
Analysis of Training and Inference Time/Cost
Evaluating Feature Quality: The AUROC of Generated Rules

outline.description: The final chapter explores the 'why' behind the performance, analyzing the impact of individual components and the framework's robustness.
subtopics: Ablation Studies: Evaluating the Impact of Reasoning and Tuning
Handling Spurious Correlations: Prior Knowledge as a Filter
Sensitivity to Hyper-parameters (Number of Rules and Ensembles)
Broader Impacts: Ethical Considerations and Societal Biases in Prior Knowledge
Future Directions: Interpretability and Larger-Scale Tabular Learning
